key_insight: He II near a wall still follows a logarithmic law of the wall, but with a distinctly nonclassical Kármán constant that stays nearly temperature-independent.
engineering_relevance: This suggests cryogenic helium-4 transport models and He II cooling hardware can use a wall-law framework, but with quantum-fluid-specific parameters instead of classical ones.
method: Measured near-wall velocity fields in mechanically driven He II pipe flow using molecular tagging velocimetry.
Independently estimated wall shear stress from pressure-drop measurements.
Compared the observed normal-fluid profile against classical logarithmic wall-law behavior across temperatures and Reynolds numbers up to 1.26×10^6.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports robust logarithmic profiles in the normal-fluid component and a nearly unchanged effective Kármán constant across the studied temperature range.
watch_item: The result is demonstrated for mechanically driven pipe flow in He II, so applying it to other geometries or forcing conditions may require new validation.
paper_title: A nonclassical law of the wall in superfluid helium-4
